title: Resolve feedback/ namespace: retired in one CLAUDE.md sentence, still live in OWNERS/code/README
Ops-folder hygiene: audit legacy scheduler/prds/ backlog and orphaned prompt-sessions top-level JSON
Build a cross-project session-manager-operations sweep skill implementing the ops-maintenance protocol
State a retention policy for feedback/archived and scheduler/prds-archived
State a retention policy for prompt-sessions/ (attachments, transcripts, archived Epic JSON)
bodyPreview:
# Goal

session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/ is 43M — by far the largest namespace under session-manager-operations/, dwarfing scheduler/ (3.0M) and feedback/ (2.9M) combined. Unlike those two (which PRD 948 already gave an explicit "keep indefinitely, no auto-prune" retention policy per ops-maintenance-protocol.md Pattern E), prompt-sessions/ has no stated retention policy anywhere: not in its own README.md, not in CLAUDE.md, not in code. It holds three growing, unbounded categories: attachments/ (pasted images, 4.8M/26 files), transcripts/ (JSONL session logs, 664K/57 files), and 50 top-level archived Epic JSON files. Nothing currently prunes any of these. Decide and document an explicit policy the same way PRD 948 did, rather than leaving this the one namespace with no answer to "how long do we keep this."

# Acceptance criteria

title: Epic-context digest builder for scheduled PRD dispatch
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Build a pure, best-effort module `src/main/lib/epicContextDigest.cjs` exporting `buildContextDigest({ cwd, epicId, maxChars })` that composes a condensed, real (never fabricated) digest of an Epic's own session, for later injection into a scheduled PRD job's opening prompt. Reuse `promptSessionTranscript.cjs`'s `readTurns(cwd, epicId, { limit })` for turn history and `epicMint.cjs`'s `readActiveIndex(cwd)` for the Epic's `goalText`/`tag` — do not reimplement transcript reading or active-index parsing. This is groundwork only: wiring it into scheduler.cjs's actual dispatch path is a separate, dependent PRD.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Wire Epic-context digest into scheduled PRD dispatch + provenance
bodyPreview:
# Goal

In `src/main/scheduler.cjs`'s job-run path, where the job's `prompt` is built from the PRD's own frontmatter body (`prompt = parsed.body + FINISH_PROTOCOL`, currently ~line 2055-2062), prepend the digest produced by PRD 950's `buildContextDigest` (from `src/main/lib/epicContextDigest.cjs`) whenever `job.epicId` resolves to an Epic in that cwd's active-index.json. This is additive only — the PRD body and FINISH_PROTOCOL suffix stay byte-for-byte unchanged, so a PRD remains fully self-contained and completable even if the digest is empty or fails to build. Also persist provenance into the run's `meta.json` sidecar so which Epic-session context (if any) a job was dispatched with is inspectable after the fact without re-deriving it, and document the new step in PRD_AUTHORING.md.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Canonical PromptSession zod schema, enforced in ensureEpic
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Today `PromptSession` (src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76) is a TypeScript-only interface with NO runtime validator anywhere. Two independent code paths hand-construct the same record shape from scratch: the renderer's `createPromptSession` (promptSessions.ts:352-364) and the main-process `ensureEpic`'s mint branch (src/main/lib/epicMint.cjs:309-329) — kept in sync only by doc comments, not by any shared schema. Create ONE canonical zod schema for the PromptSession record's content (a main-process CJS module, since zod is already a main-process dependency — see ipcSchemas.cjs:8) and make `ensureEpic` validate every session object it constructs against it before writing to active-index.json, closing the drift risk on the main-process/CLI/scheduler side first.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Enforce PromptSession schema at the IPC boundary + cross-path drift test
bodyPreview:
# Goal

PRD 952 (dependency) lands one canonical zod `PromptSessionSchema` (src/main/lib/promptSessionSchema.cjs) and wires it into `ensureEpic` (the main-process/CLI/scheduler mint path). The renderer's OWN construction path (`createPromptSession`, src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:352-364) never goes through `ensureEpic` — it sends its hand-built object over IPC via `mergeActiveIndex`, whose zod schema today validates only the envelope and treats each session's content as `z.unknown()` (src/main/ipcSchemas.cjs:217-248, `promptSessionsMergeActiveIndex`). Close that second gap: validate renderer-constructed PromptSession content against the same canonical schema at the IPC boundary, and add a regression test that would have caught the two-independently-hand-built-object-literals drift risk directly.

title: IPC handler routing Epic creation through ensureEpic (additive)
bodyPreview:

# Acceptance criteria

title: Colour the Epic timeline's PRD-dispatch chip by that PRD's live check-in status
bodyPreview:
# Goal

In an Epic's Discussion timeline, a dispatched PRD renders as a flat neutral pill — "→ dispatched to PRD #NNN" (`EpicDetail.tsx:722-733`) — that looks identical whether the PRD is still queued, finished clean, came back with a question, or failed outright. The Architect scrolling an Epic cannot tell which of its PRDs have checked back in, let alone which need action. Give that chip the traffic-light tone the rest of the app already uses: green = completed, yellow = needs_review (a question came back — act), red = failed (act), plus the existing neutral/running treatments for not-yet-checked-in. This reads the live queue snapshot that is ALREADY in scope in that component, so it needs no new plumbing and does not depend on the notification fix in PRD 972.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Surface failed / needs_review PRDs in the Epic row's rollup status so the Architect can triage 62 Epics at a glance
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`epicDisplayStatus` (`src/renderer/lib/epicDerive.ts:44`) inspects each Epic's jobs for `running` and `pending` only — it never checks `failed` or `needs_review`. So an Epic whose PRD came back broken, or parked asking a question, falls all the way through to the resting `'active'` state and renders with the same grey dot as an Epic that is simply idle. With 62 active Epics in this project, the Architect has no way to spot which ones are waiting on them without opening each one. Add two new display states so a PRD's bad outcome rolls up onto the Epic row as red and yellow, using the vocabulary already defined in `epic-primitives.tsx`'s STATUS_TONE.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Stamp PRD check-in response events with their slug + outcome so the indicator survives into the archive
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A PRD's check-in arrives on the Epic's chain as a bare `response` event with only free text (`PromptSessionEvent`, `state/promptSessions.ts:125`) — no PRD slug, no outcome. `ResponseEvent` (`EpicDetail.tsx:99`) therefore renders every check-in as the same undifferentiated grey line, and once the job is archived out of `queue.json` there is no longer ANY way to recover whether that check-in was a success, a question, or a failure — the signal is permanently lost from the Epic's audit trail. Stamp the outcome onto the event at write time in the scheduler, and tone the rendered line green/yellow/red to match the chip from PRD 974.

# Acceptance criteria

title: classifyLine becomes multi-emit and stops destroying data at classify time
bodyPreview:
# Goal

src/main/lib/classifyTranscriptLine.cjs is lossy at three verified points, and every downstream Chat/Terminal rendering improvement is blocked on fixing them. (a) The `for (const block of content)` loop `return`s on the FIRST tool_use block, so an assistant message containing text plus 3 tool calls emits ONE event and the text plus 2 calls are silently discarded. (b) The `if (obj.usage || msg?.usage)` check runs first, so any message carrying both usage and content is classified 'usage' and its content is never emitted at all. (c) `makeRaw()` keeps only `message.content`, discarding every top-level field on the line. Make classifyLine return an ARRAY of events per line, preserve the whole line, and replace classify-time string truncation with a byte-offset reference so full payloads stay recoverable without holding them in memory.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Chat view reads the JSONL transcript as its source of truth
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The Epic Chat view currently renders from chatRunner.cjs's stream-json output, which is a strictly thinner feed than the on-disk JSONL transcript. Whole classes of real session events exist ONLY in the JSONL and are therefore unreachable by Chat today — verified counts across the last 20 real sessions: attachment 317, last-prompt 252, ai-title 217, queue-operation 122, mode 94, permissionMode 24, file-history-snapshot 5. Make the JSONL tail the source of truth for the Chat view's transcript, demoting chatRunner's stream to a low-latency live tap for in-flight text only. Without this, the typed-renderer PRD downstream has no data to render.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Replace the 500-entry transcript ring buffer with indexed paged reads
bodyPreview:
# Goal

src/main/transcripts.cjs caps each subscription's in-memory buffer at 500 entries (`if (sub.buffer.length > 500) sub.buffer.shift()`) and, on first attach to a large transcript, seeks to the last 8 MB and discards everything before it (MAX_DELTA_BYTES). Both silently destroy history on any long-running Epic, which directly contradicts the Simplified Chat promise that nothing is hidden. Replace the memory buffer with an indexed, line-offset-based paged read over the transcript file so the Chat view can scroll back to the first event of a session without holding it all in RAM.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Fix PRD→Epic completion notification: resolve PRD from Epic-scoped + archived dirs, fall back to job.epicId
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`notifyOriginatingTab` in `src/main/scheduler.cjs` never routes a completed PRD's result back to its authoring Epic, because it resolves the PRD file via `prdPathForJob(job)` → `resolvePrdWriteDir(cwd)` → the RETIRED flat `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/<slug>.md`. The result is that the first and most important turn of every Epic renders in Chat as a ~2 KB prose blob with no way to know it is structured. Return the sections as data alongside the prompt, persist them on the PromptSession, and render the Epic's first turn as an AIM briefing card of labeled, individually collapsible sections.

title: Auto-recover a job that exits 0 having done nothing, instead of parking it in needs_review forever
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A headless PRD run that delegates its work to a subagent (or invokes /develop, or backgrounds a review and ends its turn) exits 0 having produced no commit and no verdict sentinel. scheduler.cjs parks that job in needs_review and stops. Nothing retries it — boot reconciliation only reaps orphaned PIDs, and the dead-process reaper only classifies runs that actually died. Recovery today is entirely manual: a human notices and hand-authors a "Fix: ..." PRD. That has now happened at least twice in this project (979 and 980; 980-chat-typed-event-renderers is parked needs_review right now while a hand-written 980-fix- sibling does its work). Make the scheduler detect this specific no-op outcome and auto-requeue the same PRD once, with the anti-self-delegation guard injected, so the common case self-heals.

title: verifyRun is handed a PRD path that does not exist — it cannot read the acceptance criteria it verifies against
bodyPreview:
# Goal

PRD 985 fixed `prdPathForJob`'s retired-flat-dir bug in the two notify functions, but left three other call sites untouched — and two of them feed the VERIFIER. `scheduler.cjs:2890` (the live post-run `verifyRun`) and `:3798` (`reverifyNeedsReview`'s `verifyRun`) both pass `prdPath = prdPathForJob(job)`, which resolves to `resolvePrdWriteDir(cwd)` — the retired flat `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/` dir that today holds only zero-byte `.reserved-NNN` stubs and no PRD at all. Every Epic-scoped PRD therefore hands the verifier a nonexistent path, so it cannot read the acceptance criteria it is supposed to verify against. This is very likely degrading verification quality on every single job, silently.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Drop `git add -A` from the finish protocol — it sweeps concurrent jobs' work into the wrong commit
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler finish protocol instructs every job to run `git add -A && git commit` (scheduler.cjs:198, restated in lib/rcaReport.cjs:84). That was safe when one job ran per project. It is not safe now that the queue can run several jobs in one working tree: whichever job commits first sweeps every sibling's in-flight edits into its own commit, mis-attributing the work and making both jobs' verdicts unreliable. Observed twice on 2026-08-02: a commit had to be hand-staged to six explicit paths to avoid capturing a concurrent job's half-written renderer files, and PRD 986's implementation was found sitting uncommitted in the tree while 986 was already archived `completed`. Replace the blanket add with explicit staging of the files the job actually changed.

# Acceptance criteria

title: The commit guard skips zero-edit runs — remove its dirty-tree precondition
bodyPreview:
# Goal

This is the half of PRD 983 that was deliberately NOT implemented in commit aa482d1 — 983 fixed the self-heal path that actually caused the PRD 972 false green, and left this latent hole open rather than rushing a riskier change. The commit guard in `spawnJob` is wrapped in `const after = await uncommittedChanges(guardCwd); if (after && after.length > 0)`, so it only ever runs when the working tree is DIRTY. A run that exits 0, commits nothing, and leaves NO newly-dirty files — the strongest possible silent-no-op signal, and exactly PRD 972's shape — bypasses `commitGuardVerdict` entirely. Close the hole without regressing the honest no-ops the guard's four existing defenses protect.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Run each scheduler job in its own git worktree so concurrent jobs cannot corrupt each other
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Now that the queue genuinely runs 4-5 jobs wide in one project, N headless agents edit ONE working tree simultaneously. Three concrete failures were observed live on 2026-08-02 with only TWO concurrent writers: a full test run showed 8 failures caused entirely by another job's half-written renderer files; a commit had to be hand-staged to avoid sweeping that job's work in; and one commit was silently rewritten to a new SHA by a concurrent rebase. Give each job its own `git worktree` checkout so its edits, its typecheck/test runs, and its commit are isolated — the same pattern this project already uses for npm publish ("publish from an isolated git worktree, never the live working directory") and that the Agent tool exposes as `isolation: worktree`.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Fix silent Epic-write rejection: register a project root before every prompt-sessions write
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Every renderer write to a project's session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/ is rejected by config.cjs's validateWrite with "Write outside allowed write boundaries" unless that project root happens to have been registered via config.addAllowedRoot() earlier in the same app run. addAllowedRoot is only called from pty.cjs (pty spawn), lib/prdCreate.cjs and projectBrief.cjs — never from the Epic persistence path. Result: right after app boot, marking an Epic Completed silently fails to persist (no tombstone, no archive) and the Epic returns as Open on the next load. Verified in ~/.config/claude-code-session-manager/logs/session-manager-2026-08-06.log (lines 45-69, 421-447) against 7 Epics completed twice on 2026-08-06 with zero disk effect.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Never report an Epic completed when its write failed: await the persist and surface the error
bodyPreview:
# Goal

markCompleted flips the in-memory status to 'completed' and fires persistActiveIndex WITHOUT awaiting it; persistActiveIndex swallows every failure into a logs.write('warn') that no user ever sees, and the subsequent archive writeJson rejection propagates into a `void`-discarded promise at EpicDetail.tsx:644. The UI therefore shows the Epic as Completed while nothing reached disk. Make the UI's data-change contract honest: the Epic is only shown Completed once the index removal AND the archive have actually landed, and any failure is surfaced through the toast channel.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Archive wins over a stale active-index row: reconcile resurrected Epics at hydrate
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Once an Epic has an archive file on disk AND a leftover row in active-index.json, it is shown Open forever with no self-healing path: hydrate() loads the active-index row as status 'active', and hydrateArchived() then skips it outright (`if (sessions[id]) continue`), so the archive is never read. Two Epics in this repo are in exactly that state right now (psess-mscdnslc-10, psess-mscg8i3u-2 — both archived 2026-08-03 with status 'completed', both still listed as 'active' in active-index.json with no tombstone). Make the archive authoritative so a partially-failed completion heals itself on the next load instead of demanding the user re-complete the Epic forever.

title: Perf P7: memo the mapped list-row components (Turn, JobRow) and stop the 1s tick re-rendering every job row

# Acceptance criteria

title: Perf P8: batch transcript events into one IPC message and one store commit per flush tick

# Goal

One JSONL line can classify into several events, and measured peak burst on a real local transcript is 11 lines in a single second, so a single flush can fan out into dozens of IPC round-trips and dozens of store notifications where one would do. Batch per flush: one message carrying the event array, one store commit applying them all.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Give the scheduler Job entity a runtime schema and make an invalid row fail loudly
bodyPreview:
# Goal

On 2026-08-07 two PRDs (1021/1022, social-signals-trader) sat unscheduled for 4+ hours because their queue.json rows carried `"status": "queued"` — a value absent from `ScheduleJobStatus` (src/preload/api.d.ts:363). Every picker filters on `status === 'pending'` exactly (scheduler.cjs:3658; schedulerBatch.cjs:94,167,198,206), so the rows were invisible, and the heartbeat's `counts[j.status] = (counts[j.status]||0)+1` (scheduler.cjs:4770) silently minted a `queued` bucket that made the bad data look like a legitimate state. The Job entity has NO runtime validation: shapeJobs (lib/queueStore.cjs:113) is `JSON.parse` + `Array.isArray` with zero field checks, and writeSplit (line 206-214) writes whatever it read straight back. Contrast the Epic entity, which has a zod schema with a status enum (lib/promptSessionSchema.cjs:58) asserted before it ever reaches disk (lib/epicMint.cjs:243). Give Job the same guarantee Epic already has.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Close the PRD-to-queue sync gap: stop the create API reporting a fake status, self-heal orphan rows, and detect a stalled queue
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A PRD is supposed to be a sub-object of the scheduler, created and managed by the scheduler MCPs — but it is not, and three concrete gaps let it drift out of sync. (1) `scheduler_create_prd` never creates a queue row: it POSTs to /admin/scheduler/create-prd, prdCreate.cjs writes only the .md file, and then returns `{ status: 'queued' }` (lib/prdCreate.cjs:243) — a status that does not exist in ScheduleJobStatus. The scheduler's own agent-facing API hands out the exact invalid string that wedged jobs 1021/1022, which is the most likely way it entered queue.json. (2) reconcile (scheduler.cjs:1305) is add-only: `if (seen.has(slug)) continue` means an existing row is never repaired, so one bad row shadows its PRD permanently. (3) Nothing detects the resulting stall — the queue sat with 2 jobs, 0 running, 0 pending for 4+ hours and the only symptom was a heartbeat count of an invented bucket. Make the create path honest, the reconcile self-healing, and the stall loud.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Route every job status change through one transition function with a legality table and an audit trail
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A job's status is assigned at 16 separate sites in scheduler.cjs (lines 723, 1741, 1802, 1808, 1819, 2863, 2908, 2963, 2985, 3072, 3272, 3359, 3457, 3705, 4128, 4166) as bare `j.status = '...'` mutations. There is no transition function, no legality table, and no record of who changed a status or why — so there is nowhere to assert that a transition is legal, and no way for the human to review status transitions after the fact. This is why the 1021/1022 stall was undiagnosable from the app: the only evidence was a heartbeat count. Introduce a single chokepoint for the Job lifecycle, mirroring how epicMint.cjs already owns the Epic's `proposed -> active` transition as the one legal path.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Complete the scheduler PRD API so direct filesystem access is no longer necessary
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Step 1 of locking the PRD entity behind the scheduler service boundary. Today the admin API exposes only FOUR routes — POST /admin/scheduler/create-prd (lib/prdCreate.cjs:219), GET /admin/scheduler/jobs (scheduler.cjs:4973), POST /admin/scheduler/reset-job (scheduler.cjs:4978) and POST /admin/chat/send-prompt (chatRunner.cjs:834). There is no way through the API to READ a PRD, LIST PRDs, EDIT one, ARCHIVE one, CANCEL or HOLD a job, or RETAG estimates. Every one of those operations therefore requires direct filesystem access today, which is precisely why direct access is still sanctioned and why the boundary leaks. A door cannot be locked while people must walk through the wall. This PRD closes the capability gap FIRST; enforcement lands only after, in the dependent PRDs — shipping enforcement before parity would break every real workflow.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Retire direct PRD authoring as the sanctioned path and fix the false retired-directory guarantee
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Direct filesystem PRD authoring is not a leak in the boundary — it is the DOCUMENTED DEFAULT. plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/SKILL.md:60 instructs "Write every PRD's markdown yourself", line 426 says "Write PRD files directly, then confirm", and lines 255-267 present `node scripts/mint-epic.cjs <cwd> <epic-id>` + a hand-written file as a first-class "manual-write fallback" co-equal with the MCP tool. The scheduler_create_prd tool description itself ends with "if the app is not running, author the PRD file by hand instead". So the service boundary is advisory by policy, not just by implementation. Separately, that same skill (lines 268-271) promises the retired flat `session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/` dir is "auto-consolidated into prds-archived/ at the next app boot WITHOUT being executed" — this is FALSE: prdLocations.cjs:126 unconditionally adds the flat dir as a live scan source, and the 2026-08-07 incident PRDs (1021/1022, social-signals-trader) were written there and did execute once their status was repaired. Consolidation only runs at boot, so anything written to the retired dir after boot stays live. Make the docs true and make the MCP the sanctioned path.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Enforce the PRD service boundary with a deny hook and API provenance stamping
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Final step of the lockdown. opsOwnership.cjs's assertOpsWrite already enforces the single-writer law (queueStore.cjs:56,64) but is structurally incapable of stopping this class of write: it guards the app's own in-process write helpers, so an agent using the Write tool bypasses it entirely — as the project CLAUDE.md itself states. Two mechanisms actually can enforce the boundary. First, a PreToolUse hook: the harness, not the app, adjudicates Write/Edit before it happens. There are currently ZERO hooks configured (both ~/.claude/settings.json and the project .claude/settings.json have an empty PreToolUse array), so this lever is entirely unused. Second, provenance: the scheduler stamps every PRD it creates, and refuses to execute one it did not create. Together these make the API the only way in, from outside and from inside.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Make the scheduler MCP reachable everywhere and teach /develop to stop rather than hand-write when it is missing
bodyPreview:
# Goal

On 2026-08-08 seven PRDs (1024-1030) in social-signals-trader were hand-written to disk between 10:00 and 10:06 and quarantined by the provenance gate. The session did not choose to bypass the API — `scheduler_create_prd` was NOT IN ITS TOOL LIST. That project's committed `.mcp.json` registers only ['burrow','quotes','hedgefund','bilko-host']; `session-manager-scheduler` was added to the working copy at 10:56, ~50 minutes AFTER the hand-writing. The natural experiment proves it: every PRD authored before 10:56 carries no provenance, and 1031/1032 authored after carry `createdVia: scheduler-api` with real `prd_create` audit records. Two fixes follow. (1) The scheduler MCP is a machine-wide service, not a per-repo dependency, so registering it once per project is the wrong shape and guarantees the next project repeats this. (2) develop/SKILL.md's fallback trigger is miscalibrated: it says the fallback applies "only when the tool errors with 'app not running' / admin API unreachable" (line 230), but an agent whose tool list lacks the tool gets NO error to match on — it just has no tool — so hand-writing is the only path it can infer. A missing tool is a MISCONFIGURATION, not an offline app, and the correct response is to stop and tell the human, never to write the file.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Make health monitoring per-project: unmask stalled projects and stop stranding quarantined PRDs
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler ENGINE is correctly machine-wide — queueStore's stateCwds() unions every project holding a queue.json plus every active project, so reconcile, the dead-process reaper, selectAutoFixTargets, spawnInvestigation, reverifyNeedsReview and the DoD drain gate all already operate across every project. The MONITORING layer did not keep up, and three gaps let a project go dark. (1) `quarantined` (shipped in the PRD-authoring lockdown) has NO automated attention and no cross-project surface: homeNeedsYou.ts:96 admits only 'failed'/'needs_review', and the 10-minute periodic pass at scheduler.cjs:4938 only fires `if (s.jobs.some(j => j.status === 'needs_review'))`. Verified live right now: the `burrow` project holds FOUR quarantined PRDs (821-ops-feedback-guard-silent-green, 822-ops-skill-graph-output-path, 823-ops-claudemd-catalog-entry, 824-ops-index-generator-versioned) that nothing will ever look at again. (2) The stall detector's verdict is global, not per-project: scheduler.cjs:991 computes `stalled = total > 0 && running === 0 && pending === 0` over the MERGED job list, so burrow being fully stalled (4 quarantined, 0 running, 0 pending) is masked by 2 running + 2 pending in other projects. It already computes `byProject` — only the boolean is wrong. (3) `npm run health` counts only `failed` (health.cjs:222), missing needs_review and quarantined entirely.

title: Fix duplicate assistant messages when a chat run ends with the SM_NEEDS_INPUT stop signal
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A long assistant reply renders TWICE in an Epic's Discussion whenever the run ends with the stop-signal protocol. Root cause: the two reconciled sources carry different text for the same message. The JSONL transcript feed holds the assistant text VERBATIM, including the trailing `<<<SM_NEEDS_INPUT>>>` + questions-JSON block; chatRunner's `chat:run:needs-input` handler pushes a turn holding only `signal.answerBody` (that same text with the sentinel block stripped by `splitStopSignal`). `turnIdentity` in `src/renderer/state/chat.ts` compares assistant turns by RAW trimmed text, so the two never match, `findRecentDuplicateTurn` returns -1, and both land in `turns`. Make assistant identity stop-signal-insensitive so the two forms collapse to one turn, and strip the sentinel block at RENDER time so the surviving turn does not show raw protocol JSON to the user.

bodyPreview:
# Goal

Three foreign keys in the Agent/WorkType/Epic/PRD/Job ERD are unvalidated strings today: `PromptSession.agentType` -> a persona file, and `ScheduleJob.epicId` / `sourcePromptId` -> an Epic. A renamed or deleted persona silently orphans every Epic pointing at it, and `agentModelResolve.cjs`'s `readPersonaModel` degrades that miss to the `sonnet` fallback without surfacing anything. Apply the agreed rule: creating a reference to something that does not exist THROWS at write time; a reference that goes dangling later is a legitimate historical state that the ops-hygiene sweep REPORTS but never breaks a read on.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Enforce the CLAUDE.md size budget as an automated check
bodyPreview:
# Goal

CLAUDE.md grew unchecked from 3,871 to 65,768 chars between 2026-05-09 and 2026-08-13 — it is read on every turn of every session, so that was ~17k tokens of standing overhead per turn. RCA (2026-08-24): 57 feature commits appended to it and, across 359 PRDs, exactly zero ever pruned it; 7 of the 8 `docs(claude-md)` "cleanup" commits actually GREW the file. The file was split down to ~11.9k chars and now declares a 12,000-char SIZE BUDGET in its own header, but that budget is currently enforced only by agents remembering to read it. Make it a machine check so the regression is caught the moment it happens rather than 54k chars later.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Stop historyAggregatorPricing's remote.aggregate test scanning the real 5.2GB transcript corpus
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`tests/unit/historyAggregatorPricing.spec.ts`'s `remote.aggregate > returns the existing result shape plus per-model costUsd and a top-level cacheSavingsUsd` calls `remote.aggregate({})` with no filter, which scans the developer's REAL `~/.claude/projects` transcript tree — currently 5.2 GB across 52,583 .jsonl files — against a hardcoded 15,000 ms timeout (spec line 120; vitest.config.ts:16 sets the same global). This is not a flaky test, it is a test with an unbounded real-data dependency that gets monotonically slower every session. Measured 2026-08-26: 3.35 s in isolation, 15,022 ms (FAIL) under full-suite CPU contention. It is already at the edge and will fail permanently as the corpus grows. Make it hermetic so it measures the aggregator's logic instead of the machine's transcript history.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Make a PRD's WorkType settable at creation and consistent across both write paths
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Epic and PRD both carry a WorkType tag drawn from one shared enum (PRD 1036), but they are INDEPENDENT values: an Epic is the plan, a PRD is one unit of work inside it, and a single plan legitimately contains several different work types. That independence is already true in the write path — prdCreate.cjs passes `tag` straight through and nothing derives it from the parent Epic. What is missing is the ability to SET it: `scheduler_create_prd` exposes no `tag` property at all, so every PRD authored through the only sanctioned path is born untagged. Expose it, and make the two PRD write paths agree on which values are legal.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Field Manual: add the 4 missing tab chapters so every nav destination is covered
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The Field Manual claims to be a tab-by-tab operator's guide, but 4 of the 18 nav destinations in `NAV_ITEMS` have no chapter of their own: File Explorer (`projects`, the only item on BOTH faces), Plugins, System Prompt, and Host on Bilko.run. Verified by grep — "File Explorer" appears in zero chapters; the other three appear only as passing mentions inside unrelated chapters. Write the 4 missing chapters so a buyer opening any tab in the app can find the page that explains it.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Field Manual: write capture recipes for all 23 figure slots so the screenshot run is one command
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The annotated-screenshot pipeline already exists and does exactly what is wanted — `scripts/capture-manual-figures.mjs` drives the real app under Playwright, resolves each callout to a live bounding box, and composites numbered arrow callouts onto a real screenshot. It is starved of input: the manual declares 19 figure slots (23 after PRD 1042) but `figure-captures.json` holds only 4 recipes, so 0 PNGs have ever been produced and every chapter still shows an empty placeholder frame. Write the missing recipes so one `npm run manual:figures` run captures every figure.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Ship scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs in the npm package
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler MCP server file is NOT included in the published npm tarball. `package.json`'s `files` array ships `scripts/lib/`, `scripts/postinstall.cjs` and `scripts/mint-epic.cjs` but omits `scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs`. Verified: `npm pack --dry-run` lists only those four script paths. Consequence: on any machine that installed via `npx claude-code-session-manager`, the `scheduler_create_prd` MCP tool can never be registered, so agents silently fall back to implementing inline instead of queueing PRDs. Add the file (and every local file it requires) to `files`, and add a packaging regression test so it can never be dropped again.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Ship default architect + dev-lead agent personas and seed them on first boot
bodyPreview:
# Goal

No Agent personas ship with the app. `architect.md` and `dev-lead.md` exist only in one developer's `~/.claude/agents/` directory; `grep -rn "DEFAULT_AGENT|defaultPersona|seedAgents|builtinAgents" src/` returns zero hits. On a fresh install the Agent Library is empty, so a user cannot select the Architect persona at all and every Epic runs with no Actor. Ship both personas inside the package and seed them into `~/.claude/agents/` on first boot, using the same marker+bounded-retry idempotency pattern as the existing dev-plugin seeder.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Rewrite the feature/bug Mission templates to mandate /develop delegation
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The `feature` Mission tag actively instructs the opposite of the intended workflow. `src/renderer/lib/agentTagDefs.ts:26-30` sends "You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end..." as the first framing line of every feature Epic. Meanwhile `plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/SKILL.md` declares that for `feature`/`bug` Epics "decomposition into PRDs is the expected default path". The tag is delivered on every Epic; the skill's rule is only read if the skill is invoked. So the loudest instruction in the session says implement inline. Rewrite the `feature` and `bug` `initialPromptTemplate`s so they frame the session as plan-and-delegate, pointing at `/develop`, without forking the skill's mechanics.

# Acceptance criteria

title: PreToolUse hook: deny inline Write/Edit to app source in feature/bug Epics
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Prompt-level instructions to delegate are advisory; nothing currently catches an interactive Epic that implements inline anyway. The repo already proves the lever works: `scripts/hooks/guard-prd-writes.cjs` is a PreToolUse hook that denies raw Write/Edit under `session-manager-operations/scheduler/**` precisely because in-app ownership checks are "structurally incapable of stopping an agent that reaches for the Write tool directly". Build the sibling guard: in a `feature`/`bug` Epic, deny a Write/Edit/NotebookEdit against application source and tell the agent to queue the work via `/develop` instead. Ships enabled by default, with an explicit per-Epic escape hatch for deliberate inline work.

# Acceptance criteria

title: First-boot seeder: register the scheduler MCP server at user scope
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler MCP server is registered today only via this one repo's `.mcp.json`, with a relative path (`scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs`) that resolves nowhere else. Every other project on the machine, and every fresh install, therefore has no `scheduler_create_prd` tool — the documented cause of agents hand-writing or inline-implementing instead of queueing (see the header of `scripts/install-scheduler-mcp-user-scope.sh`). That installer already exists as a manual bash script; promote it to an automatic first-boot seeder at USER scope, since the server is a machine-wide service that talks to the app's loopback admin API, not anything project-specific.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Delegation-readiness probe: is the PRD pipeline actually installed?
bodyPreview:
# Goal

When the scheduler MCP server is not registered, `scheduler_create_prd` is simply absent from the agent's tool list — there is no error to catch, so the agent experiences a vacuum and quietly implements inline instead. This is a documented repeat incident (see the header of `scripts/install-scheduler-mcp-user-scope.sh`, PRD 1024-1030). Build a main-process probe that answers "can this project actually delegate?" as structured data, so the absence becomes a stated fact rather than a silent gap. This PRD delivers the probe and its IPC handler only; surfacing it in the UI and in the Epic's grounding line is a dependent PRD.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Add a delegate-implementation Context Injection, default-on for feature/bug
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The delegation law needs to hold even when the Agent Library is empty and no persona resolved — which is the state of every fresh install. `CONTEXT_INJECTIONS` (src/renderer/lib/contextInjections.ts) exists exactly for this: Session-Manager-authored prompt text independent of which persona or Mission tag was chosen, described in its own header as "the floor every session stands on, including Epics created before any persona resolved". Today it has a single entry, `general-behavior`. Add a second, `delegate-implementation`, carrying the plan-and-queue rule, toggled on by default for `feature`/`bug` Epics in the New Epic card.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Per-Epic delegation counter: PRDs queued vs inline edits made
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Whether Epics actually delegate is currently anecdotal — the only evidence is a human noticing after the fact. Make it measurable: show, per Epic, how many PRDs it authored versus how many source files it edited inline, so drift is visible on the Epic card instead of discovered weeks later on a different machine.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Add a delegation-chain check to npm run health
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Make the "can this machine actually delegate work to the scheduler?" question answerable in one command, on any machine, without opening the app. `npm run health` (`src/main/health.cjs`) is the existing entry point for `/local-project-health` and exits 0 for GREEN. Add a delegation-chain section that reports the four readiness checks, so this class of misconfiguration is caught by a routine health run rather than by a human noticing weeks later that Epics stopped queueing PRDs.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Surface delegation readiness in the New Epic card and in the Epic's grounding line
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Consume the `app:delegation-readiness` probe so a broken PRD pipeline is visible to the human BEFORE they open an Epic, and stated to the agent INSIDE the Epic. The second half matters most: a missing MCP tool is otherwise an absence the agent cannot perceive, so it silently implements inline instead. Folding the readiness result into the Epic's AIM "Input" grounding line converts that vacuum into a stated fact.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Surface first-boot seeder failures in the UI instead of only console.warn
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Every first-boot seeder fails silently. `src/main/seedDevPlugin.cjs` gives up after 3 attempts and only calls `logger.warn`, so a user whose dev plugin never installed has no way to know `/develop` is missing — they just experience an agent that implements inline. The same is true for the new scheduler-MCP and agent-persona seeders. Make an exhausted or failed seed visible in the app, with the manual fix.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Inject the Agent persona's body into the Epic opening prompt, not just its description
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Every Agent persona's operating rules are dead text today. `composeEpicIntake` (src/renderer/lib/epicIntake.ts:150-158) emits an Actor section containing ONLY the persona's frontmatter `description` one-liner; the persona markdown BODY is never sent to the session. Claude Code only loads a persona body when the file is run as a subagent, and an Epic's main loop never is. So the architect persona's central law — "never hand-implement inline in this conversation, queue via /develop" — is written down and delivered nowhere, which is the direct cause of Architect Epics implementing inline. Add a `persona-body` section to the AIM Actor axis carrying the persona's markdown body (frontmatter stripped), capped at 6000 characters with an explicit truncation notice.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Data Model ERD part 1 of 3 - dataModelErd lib with entities relations layout and integrity test
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Create `src/renderer/lib/dataModelErd.ts` — a hand-maintained, code-grounded description of every entity Session Manager actually persists (real file paths, real field names, real single-writer owners), plus the explicit relation edge list and a PURE deterministic layout function for drawing it. This is the data layer for a new "Data Model" screen that parts 2 and 3 of this chain will render and wire up; it ships with a unit test that fails on a dangling reference. No React and no UI in this PRD.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Data Model ERD part 2 of 3 - DataModel screen with interactive diagram and entity detail
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Build `src/renderer/components/tabs/DataModel.tsx` — the screen that renders the ERD from `lib/dataModelErd.ts`: an SVG diagram of every entity box and relation edge, a Tables view with the full field list per entity, and a detail pane showing one entity's storage path, single-writer owner, every field with pk/fk markers, and its relations as clickable links to the related entity. title: Data Model ERD part 3 of 3 - wire the Data Model tab into the Home face and document it
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Make the Data Model ERD reachable as a real application tab on the HOME face: add the `data-model` NavKey, register the screen, give it a sidebar row under Tools, add a Home entry-point card, and record it in the architecture docs. After this PRD a user pressing the Home-face sidebar row (or the Home card) lands on the ERD screen with the sidebar staying on the Home face.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Auto-fix plans must be written to the failed job's Epic-scoped prds dir, not the retired flat dir
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler's self-heal is structurally incapable of ever landing a fix plan. `spawnInvestigation` computes `fixPath` as `path.join(prdDirForCwd(failedJob.cwd), `${fixSlug}.md`)` (src/main/scheduler.cjs:3181), which resolves to the RETIRED flat `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/` dir. `reconcile()` calls `consolidateAllFlatPrds()` at src/main/scheduler.cjs:1368 — deliberately BEFORE the on-disk PRD scan — and that sweep archives any flat-dir `.md` whose slug is not already a live queue row. A freshly-authored fix plan has no queue row yet by definition, so every auto-fix plan is moved to `prds-archived/` on the very next reconcile pass (~60s) and is never enqueued. Confirmed live in /home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships: job `105-arena-perf-fences` sat in needs_review with `autoFixAttempted: true`; its investigation ran 02:52:40Z-02:55:25Z and DID produce a valid 24KB fix plan, which now sits in `session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds-archived/105-fix-arena-perf-fences.md` having never appeared in queue.json or history.jsonl. Fix: write the fix plan into the SAME dir the original PRD lives in (its Epic-scoped `epics/<epicId>/prds/`), which `resolvePrdsDirs` already scans as a first-class source and which `consolidateFlatPrds` never touches.

# Acceptance criteria

title: A needs_review job whose auto-fix produced a plan that never landed is silently stranded — close the eligibility/annotation gap
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Self-heal has a terminal state it neither retries nor reports. `selectAutoFixTargets` (src/main/scheduler.cjs:4432) excludes any job with `autoFixAttempted === true` unless `autoFixOutcome === 'no-plan'`. `autoFixOutcome` is only ever stamped in the ELSE branch of `if (fs.existsSync(fixPath))` in `spawnInvestigation`'s onExit (src/main/scheduler.cjs:3311) — i.e. only when NO plan was produced. So a job whose investigation DID produce a plan, but whose plan then failed to become a queue row for any reason, ends up with `autoFixAttempted: true` and `autoFixOutcome: undefined`: permanently ineligible for retry. The compensating "surface the dead-ends" annotation at src/main/scheduler.cjs:4570-4573 gates on the SAME `autoFixOutcome === 'no-plan'`, so the job is not flagged `autofix_no_plan` either. Result: it sits in needs_review forever with no retry, no annotation, and no log line — exactly the observed starry-night-ships symptom (`105-arena-perf-fences`, needs_review since 2026-08-30T02:52Z, `autoFixAttempted: true`, no outcome field). Even with the sibling PRD fixing the write path, this gap must close so any future non-landing failure mode is visible rather than silent.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Add a terminal `skipped` job status so a never-run PRD is never reported as `completed`
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A queue row whose PRD source file has vanished from disk is currently retired to the terminal status `completed` — the exact same status a genuinely successful executor run produces. Confirmed at src/main/scheduler.cjs:3495, which fires for ANY truthy `res.skipped`, including the `prd-missing` reason built at src/main/scheduler.cjs:637. Real incident (2026-08-30, project /home/bilko/Projects/sigma): 20 queued PRDs went pending -> running -> completed via `spawnJob:skip-archived` with reason "PRD source no longer exists on disk — retiring stale queue entry"; none ever spawned an executor, none wrote code, yet every consumer read them as shipped and a whole PR-review round was reported finished when nothing had happened. Add a distinct terminal status `skipped` and route the never-ran case to it so unrun work can never masquerade as done.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Paginate GET /admin/scheduler/prds and trim its body by default
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`GET /admin/scheduler/prds` (src/main/lib/prdAdminRoutes.cjs:47-57) serialises the entire result of `remote.listPrds(input)` in one response with no limit, offset, or field trimming. Reported 2026-08-30 by an agent monitoring the sigma queue: the unfiltered call returned roughly 353 KB and timed out at 120 s via curl, making the endpoint effectively unusable for the exact case it exists for — an agent asking "what PRDs are there". Add cursor/limit pagination and stop shipping full PRD bodies unless asked, so the default response is small and fast.

# Acceptance criteria

title: clear-queue must write a history row for every job it removes
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The `schedule:clear-queue` IPC handler at src/main/scheduler.cjs:4938-4944 deletes every non-running job row straight out of `state.jobs` with `s.jobs = s.jobs.filter(...)` and never appends anything to history.jsonl. A job can therefore leave the queue with zero audit trail: it simply vanishes. Observed 2026-08-30 in /home/bilko/Projects/sigma, where the queue row `788-pr-sweep-final-gate` disappeared from the live jobs list with no record at all in state/history.jsonl (verified: `grep -c 788-pr-sweep-final-gate history.jsonl` returns 0, while its 20 siblings each have a row). Anyone reconstructing what happened to a queue from history.jsonl gets a silently incomplete picture. Every removal from the queue must leave a durable, attributable history row.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Sweep the executor's process group after a normal exit so orphaned test batteries cannot survive the job
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Scheduler jobs are spawned `detached: true` and every WATCHDOG path (result-tail, deadman, idle-tail) kills the whole process group via ctx.killTree. But when the executor child exits NORMALLY, nothing sweeps the group — any process the agent backgrounded (the `bash -c '<gate> > /tmp/x.log; echo $? > /tmp/x.done'` shape agents use to work around the foreground call cap) reparents to init and keeps running for nobody. Measured 2026-08-31 in ~/Projects/starry-night-ships: three orphaned full test batteries at PPID 1, one burning ~5 cores for 56 minutes. Add a post-exit group sweep so a job's descendants die with the job.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Job worktree isolation must not be silently defeated by an untracked file
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Per-job `git worktree` isolation (PRD 994) is on by default, but `isBaseTreeClean` in src/main/lib/gitWorktree.cjs runs `git status --porcelain`, which counts UNTRACKED files. A single stray untracked file in a project therefore disables worktree isolation for EVERY scheduler job in that project, permanently and silently (one console.log line). Confirmed live on 2026-08-31 in ~/Projects/starry-night-ships: `git status --porcelain` there is exactly one line, `?? scripts/dev/_scratch_bbox.gd.uid`, `git worktree list` shows no job worktrees, and two commits on that branch (534a916, c0d37fb) each carry a different PRD's work spliced in — the exact cross-contamination isolation exists to prevent. The failure is also self-reinforcing: a job that fails to commit leaves the tree dirty, which disables isolation for all later jobs. Make untracked files stop defeating isolation, and make any remaining fallback loudly visible instead of console-only.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Commit guard: an isolated worktree run must not be excused by the siblingRunning carve-out
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The inbound report asked for a check that a `completed` verdict is backed by a real commit. That check already exists — `commitGuardVerdict` in src/main/scheduler.cjs compares HEAD before/after and the newly-dirty file set, and downgrades to needs_review with verdict `silent_no_op` or `uncommitted_changes`. But it has four carve-outs, and the FIRST one (`siblingRunning`) disables it entirely whenever another job is running in the same cwd — which is precisely the high-concurrency situation where false "completed" verdicts are most likely, and which is exactly how the reported PRD 109 shipped as `completed` with nothing committed. That carve-out exists because a shared working tree makes dirt unattributable. When the job ran in its OWN worktree, the evidence IS attributable and the excuse does not apply.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Tighten the auto-fix chain cap from three fix jobs to two
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The inbound report claimed `-fix-` chains grow without bound. That is wrong — src/main/scheduler.cjs already caps them: `MAX_INVESTIGATION_DEPTH = 2` and `isFixPlanBeyondDepthCap` excludes a fix-plan job from auto-fix eligibility once investigationDepth >= 3. The three live chains they cited (115-fix-fix, 113-fix-fix, 111-fix-fix-fix) sit at or just under that existing cap, so the cap is working; the question is whether it is set too high. Their evidence says yes: they read the 115-fix-fix prompt and its own root-cause section reads "The code was already CORRECT. Only verification and commit failed." A third auto-retry re-runs an entire expensive PRD and a full test battery to redo a `git commit`, at near-zero marginal success probability. Lower the cap to two fix jobs per original slug.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Fix stale cross-project delegation-readiness in NewEpicCard
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The New Session card renders ANOTHER project's "Delegation not ready" banner. `src/renderer/components/epics/NewEpicCard.tsx:245-256` fetches `window.api.app.delegationReadiness(effectiveCwd)` inside a `useEffect` with an EMPTY dependency array while reading `effectiveCwd`, so the result is frozen at whatever cwd resolved on the card's first render. `EpicsWorkspace.tsx:64` keeps `showNewEpic` true across project-tab switches and mounts `NewEpicCard` without a `key`, so the card survives a cwd change: the "Project" line at `NewEpicCard.tsx:452` updates live while `readiness` does not. Reproduced 2026-08-31: `checkDelegationReadiness` returns `ok:true` for `/home/bilko/Projects/session-manager` and `ok:false` (failing `prd-write-guard`) for `/home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships`, and the starry-night-ships fix line was displayed on a different project's card. Make the readiness probe track `effectiveCwd` so the banner can only ever describe the project the card is currently scoped to.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Per-project concurrent-job cap so one CPU-bound test battery cannot share a machine with itself
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The inbound report claimed there is no concurrency cap. That is wrong — src/main/lib/sessionSlots.cjs is a machine-wide pool (default 5, range [0,10], SM_SESSION_SLOTS override) and spawnJob already refuses to dispatch without a slot. The real gap is that the cap is GLOBAL and blind to the project: 4 of the 5 slots can all land on the same project, and if that project's gate is a CPU-bound test battery they contend with each other. Measured 2026-08-31 in ~/Projects/starry-night-ships: 4 executors, loadavg 25.89 on 14 cores, one test process at 522% CPU for 30 minutes, and that project's timing tests SELF-DOWNGRADE under load ("CONTENDED: 14 timing checks reported but not enforced, load/core 1.92 > 0.50") — so concurrency silently converts a real performance gate into a no-op. Add a per-project cap on top of the existing global pool.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Emit an absolute guard-script path in the prd-write-guard readiness fix
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`checkPrdWriteGuard` in `src/main/lib/delegationReadiness.cjs` (~line 113) tells the user to install a PreToolUse hook running `node scripts/hooks/guard-prd-writes.cjs` — a RELATIVE path that only resolves when the hook's cwd is the session-manager repo itself. The guard script lives only in session-manager, so following that instruction in any other project installs a hook that fails on every Write/Edit. Reproduced 2026-08-31: the New Session card scoped to `~/Projects/starry-night-ships` renders exactly that fix string, and that repo has no `scripts/hooks/` directory and no `.claude/settings.json` at all. The script's own header (`scripts/hooks/guard-prd-writes.cjs:40-46`) already documents that a non-session-manager project MUST reference it by ABSOLUTE path, so the probe currently contradicts the artifact it points at. Make the fix string emit an absolute path, matching what `checkSchedulerMcp` in the same file already does.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Dump a failed job worktree's uncommitted diff to the run directory before teardown
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A scheduler job that dies before its finish-protocol commit loses every uncommitted edit in its isolated worktree. scheduler.cjs's finally block captures only the PATH LIST of leftover dirty files (worktreeLeftoverDirty = await uncommittedChanges(worktree.dir)) and then calls cleanupJobWorktree, which removes the checkout — the file CONTENT is destroyed, with no branch, no stash, and no patch anywhere. Confirmed live 2026-09-01 for PRD 131 in starry-night-ships: ~12 minutes of work, 7 Edits, killed during verification with no verdict; the diff only survived because the app was down so cleanup never ran. Fix: write the worktree's full diff (tracked + untracked) into the run directory before teardown, so any late-run failure — rate limit, timeout, crash, kill — is recoverable.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Ban backgrounded verification and wait-for-notification tools in the scheduler finish protocol
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Headless executors keep burning whole runs by starting a verification command as a BACKGROUND task and then waiting for a completion notification (TaskOutput block:true, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). There is no later turn in a `claude -p` run, so the harness stops the task and the run dies mid-verification with no SCHEDULER_VERDICT and no commit — exactly what killed PRD 131 in starry-night-ships on 2026-09-01 (a `timeout 900` test script backgrounded, then TaskOutput(block:true, timeout 590000), then a stopped task and exit 144). That project's CLAUDE.md already documents three prior runs lost the same way, but per-repo documentation only reaches repos that wrote it. FINISH_PROTOCOL in src/main/scheduler.cjs is appended to EVERY scheduled job prompt in every project, so the rule belongs there.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Normalize a git-worktree cwd to its main project root in activeSessions (worktree cwds are being registered as projects; the real project vanishes)
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`scripts/lib/activeSessions.cjs` reads the LAST `cwd` row of each project dir's newest transcript. When an Epic or job runs in a managed git worktree, that cwd is `/tmp/session-manager-epic-worktrees/<hash>/<epicId>` (or the job equivalent) — an absolute, existing directory — so `addCwd` accepts it as a project and the REAL project root is never added at all. Verified live on 2026-09-01: `allProjectCwds()` returned 21 cwds including `/tmp`, `/tmp/session-manager-epic-worktrees/443997d5bbc5f8ab/enemies-animation-adopt-the-same-model-as-the-sp-8e84c8c8` and two `/tmp/session-manager-job-worktrees/...` paths, while `/home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships` was MISSING — so `resolvePrdsDirs()` returned 0 dirs for that project, its 9 queued jobs were absent from `GET /admin/scheduler/jobs`, and `scheduler_reset_job('133-enemy-crew-body-adoption')` failed with `invalid slug`. This PRD teaches `projectRootOf` to resolve a worktree cwd back to its main tree, and to drop a tmp-root cwd it cannot resolve.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Purge the ops-state stubs already materialized under /tmp worktrees, and refuse to write project state into a worktree or tmpdir
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Because worktree cwds were accepted as projects, `queueStore.writeSplit` materialized per-project scheduler state inside EPHEMERAL git worktrees — verified live 2026-09-01: `/tmp/session-manager-epic-worktrees/443997d5bbc5f8ab/enemies-animation-adopt-the-same-model-as-the-sp-8e84c8c8/session-manager-operations/scheduler/state/queue.json` was being rewritten every reconcile pass (mtime tracked the clock, content `{"jobs":[]}`), plus two job-worktree ops trees and a stray `/tmp/session-manager-operations/logs/`. A worktree is torn down when its Epic/job ends, so any state written there is silently destroyed. This PRD removes the existing stubs and adds a fail-closed guard so a state path under `os.tmpdir()` or inside a linked git worktree is never written again, even if a future discovery bug reintroduces such a cwd.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Scheduler MCP: replace the misleading "invalid slug" with a real not-found error, and accept a cwd hint on reset/cancel/archive
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`POST /admin/scheduler/reset-job` with a perfectly well-formed slug returns `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid slug"}` whenever the PRD file is not found in any scannable PRD directory (`scheduler.cjs:5062` — `safeSlugPath` returns null for BOTH a malformed slug and a slug that exists nowhere). Agents read that as "I typed it wrong", retry, then give up and ask the human — exactly what happened on 2026-09-01 with `133-enemy-crew-body-adoption`. Split the two conditions into distinct, actionable errors, and give `scheduler_reset_job` / `scheduler_cancel_job` / `scheduler_archive_prd` the optional `cwd` hint that `scheduler_get_prd` / `scheduler_update_prd` already accept.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Reap a pidless zombie: a running row whose spawn never recorded runtime.pid is currently immortal
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`reapDeadRunningJobs` bails on `if (!pid) continue` (`scheduler.cjs:4218`) with the comment "spawn may be mid-flight; give it a cycle" — but there is no age bound, so a row that NEVER records `runtime.pid` is skipped on every cycle forever. Verified live 2026-09-01: `1076-mcp-tool-catalog-single-source` sat `running` for 464 minutes against a 24-minute estimate with no `runtime` key, no `claude -p` process, and an EMPTY run directory (`runs/2026-09-01T10-56-22-538Z/` created 03:56, zero files) — the row was marked running with a runId and startedAt before the spawn, and the spawn never got far enough to record a pid. Every other safety net is pid- or child-bound (the 4h deadman and the 20-min idle watchdog are timers on the live child, `scheduler.cjs:2928`; the supervisor probes `j.runtime?.pid`, `:5247`/`:5265`), and `findOverrunningJobs` is escalation-only by design (`:1122` "never kill on an estimate"). So nothing on the machine can ever clear such a row. Give the reaper an age-bounded pidless path.

# Acceptance criteria

title: One MCP tool catalog as the single source of truth for tool descriptions, recipes and demos
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Sessions repeatedly fail to work the Session Manager MCP surface correctly because the only description of these 13 tools is the inline `description` strings inside `scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs`'s `TOOLS` array — invisible to the app, to the Home tab, to the manual, and to a human debugging why a session went off-piste. Extract a `src/main/lib/mcpToolCatalog.cjs` that owns, per tool: name, one-line purpose, when-to-use, when-NOT-to-use, a runnable example argument object, and the common multi-tool recipes (queue a PRD, unstick a job, hand a finding to another project). `scheduler-mcp-server.cjs` then BUILDS its tool descriptions from the catalog so the two can never drift, and a new admin route exposes it to the renderer.

# Acceptance criteria

title: "investigating" has no watchdog: a job parked there by a dead app instance never leaves it
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`spawnInvestigation` sets a job to `investigating` (`scheduler.cjs:3331`) and restores its prior status on probe exit (`:3376`) or on a spawn throw (`:3442`) — both of which only run inside the live process. The code comments already assert "'investigating' must never be the job's resting state" (`:3373`), but nothing enforces that across an app restart: if the app dies while a probe is out, the row stays `investigating` forever. Verified live 2026-09-01: burrow's `834-session-summary-reports-planner-intent-as-outcome` had been `investigating` for 1653 minutes (27.5 hours) even though the row itself carries `finishedAt: 2026-08-31T15:13:15.181Z` and `exitCode: 0` — it had actually finished 27 hours earlier. Neither reaper looks at it: `reapDeadRunningJobs` and `findOverrunningJobs` both start with `if (j.status !== 'running') continue`.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Fix: finish and commit the Home tab Agent tools block (PRD 1077 self-scheduled instead of verifying)
bodyPreview:
# Read this first — why the previous run failed

The previous run of PRD `1077-home-tab-agent-tools-block` **wrote almost all of the code and then
threw it away by waiting**. Quoting the canonical rule verbatim from
`plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/standards.md`:

title: session_manager_help MCP tool: give agents the same catalog the Home tab shows, and point every error at it
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The Home tab is a HUMAN surface — a headless `claude -p` session never sees it. The sessions that keep mis-driving these tools need the catalog in a channel they actually read, so expose it as a first-class MCP tool: `session_manager_help({ topic?, tool? })` returns the same `mcpToolCatalog` data — the tool list with when-to-use / when-NOT-to-use, the multi-tool recipes, and this project's delegation-readiness state — and every failure path in the scheduler MCP server appends a one-line pointer to it. An agent that gets an error learns the right next call from the error itself instead of asking the human.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Resolve the true project root and owning Epic server-side for every MCP mutation, so a session inside a worktree stops being refused
bodyPreview:
# Goal

An agent running inside an Epic's git worktree has `pwd` = `/tmp/session-manager-epic-worktrees/<hash>/<epicId>` and naturally passes that as `cwd` to `scheduler_create_prd` / `feedback_open_session`. `prdCreate.cjs`'s `resolveSourcePromptIdFromClaudeSession(cwd, id)` then reads `<worktree>/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/active-index.json` — a git-tracked snapshot frozen at branch time. Verified live 2026-09-01 on starry-night-ships: main's index has 5 rows including the running Epic; the worktree's copy has 1 row and does NOT contain it, so resolution returns null and the write is refused with "create/approve an Epic first". To the human this reads as "the Epic got lost" and "the MCP doesn't work for sessions". Move project-root and Epic resolution SERVER-SIDE: normalize any supplied cwd to its main tree, and when `originClaudeSessionId` is present, find the owning Epic across every known project rather than only the cwd the agent guessed.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Make the Epic index rebuildable from the Epic files: status mirror on every Epic JSON, a rebuild path, and a health check for index/file drift
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`active-index.json` is the ONLY place an Epic's `status` lives; the per-Epic `prompt-sessions/<id>.json` has no `status` field at all (verified: `delegation-readiness-...json` → `status: None`). Counted live 2026-09-01: session-manager has 126 Epic files vs 1 index row, Bilko 9 files vs 0 rows, signal-builder 0 files vs 1 row. So a lost, clobbered, git-reverted or worktree-snapshotted index silently erases every Epic it held, and there is no way to get them back — "I keep losing Epics". Make the index a derived view: every transition mirrors `status`/`archivedAt`/`cwd` onto the Epic file, a `rebuildActiveIndex(cwd)` reconstructs rows from files (honoring tombstones), boot uses it when the index is missing or unreadable, and health/ops-sweep report drift instead of letting it accumulate.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Delegation readiness must prove the scheduler MCP server actually answers, and self-repair a registration whose script path is gone
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`checkDelegationReadiness` answers "is `session-manager-scheduler` registered" by checking that a key exists in `~/.claude.json` and that the script path resolves — it never proves the server starts or that `scheduler_create_prd` is in its tool list. A registration can be present and dead (repo moved, node missing from PATH, a syntax error in the server, an `.mcp.json` project entry with a RELATIVE path `scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs` shadowing the absolute user-scope one — this repo has exactly that duplicate today with `enabledMcpjsonServers: []`), and every one of those shows GREEN while sessions silently lose the tool. Add a real liveness probe (spawn the registered command, send `tools/list`, require `scheduler_create_prd`), make `seedSchedulerMcp` repair a user-scope entry whose script no longer exists, flag project-scope duplicates, and surface all of it in the New Epic banner, `session_manager_help`, and `npm run health`.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Gate job launches on machine load, not just memory: no new executor while 1-min loadavg per core is over the threshold
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler gates launches on free memory (`availableForJobs`/`memoryLimitedBatchSize`) and, once published, on a static per-project cap of 2 (`schedulerConfig.projectJobCap`, written against the 2026-08-31 loadavg-25.89 incident). Neither looks at CPU. Observed 2026-09-01 19:25 on starry-night-ships: 4 concurrent executors each running a Godot test battery under its own Xvfb, loadavg 12.95 on 14 cores. Under that contention every 8-minute battery stretches, executors hit their own `timeout`, the verifier files `FAIL/FATAL (no self-recovery)` → `needs_review` → an auto-fix chain with inflated estimates (155: 25 → 150 → 110 min) that launches MORE batteries. A static cap cannot see this feedback loop; a load-average gate can. Add one, escalation-visible, layered under the existing pool exactly the way the per-project cap is.

Every namespace under `session-manager-operations/` computes its own path with a bare `path.join(cwd, 'session-manager-operations', ...)`: `epicMint.activeIndexPath`, `queueStore.projectStateDir`, `prdLocations.resolvePrdWriteDir/resolveEpicsRoot`, `opsErrorLog.todayFile`, `projectBrief`, and more. # Acceptance criteria

title: Scheduler: per-project starvation escalation in the heartbeat
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The NN-ordering starvation bug (PRD 1086) went unnoticed for 3.5 hours because nothing in the scheduler distinguishes "this project has no pending work" from "this project has pending work and has been passed over on every tick while other projects dispatched". The existing heartbeat/escalation family (findStaleQuarantinedJobs, findOverrunningJobs, findStrandedInvestigations) covers stuck ROWS but has no signal for an entirely passed-over PROJECT. Add a pure `findStarvedProjects()` predicate plus a heartbeat escalation so any future regression in cross-project fairness is visible within minutes instead of requiring a human to notice.

# Acceptance criteria

statusHistory.reason: manual archive of an already-shipped PRD

title: Scheduler: fair cross-project slot allocation (stop NN-number starvation)
bodyPreview:
# Goal

pickNextBatch() in src/main/lib/schedulerBatch.cjs sorts projects for slot allocation by `lowestPendingForProject` = the minimum `parallelGroup` (per-project NN) among their pending jobs, ascending. NN numbers are allocated PER PROJECT (scheduler.cjs allocateParallelGroup -> prdDirForCwd(cwd)) and are monotonically increasing, so this compares unrelated sequences: a project with a long PRD history always sorts behind a young project, and starves indefinitely while the young project keeps queueing. Confirmed live on 2026-09-01: social-signals-trader (8 pending, lowest NN 3887) got zero starts for 3.5h while starry-night-ships (lowest NN 158) took every freed slot. Replace the cross-project ordering with a fairness rule that is independent of numbering, AND hand slots out round-robin instead of draining one project to its cap first. Within a project, parallelGroup ordering stays exactly as-is (a priority hint).

title: Ship the Project Pages pipeline assets in the npm package, gated on freshness

title: Expose the Project Home contract as four MCP tools on the scheduler server
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Add four MCP tools to the session-manager-scheduler server — project_home_get_contract, project_home_validate_summary, project_home_render and project_home_status — as thin wrappers over the admin routes landed by PRD 1089. This is the surface the generating session actually calls, and it is what makes the feature work on a machine that has only the npm package: the session asks the app for the contract and calls back through these tools instead of reading session-manager's repo.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Seed a portable project-home-builder persona and rewrite the Epic prompt to use the MCP contract
bodyPreview:
# Goal

On a foreign machine the project-home-builder Epic starts with no persona at all (src/seed/agents/ ships only architect.md and dev-lead.md, so agents.listPersonas() never finds it) and with a grounding prompt pointing at four repo-local paths that do not exist.
