Ship a portable persona, make the seeder able to deliver it to already-installed machines, and rewrite the prompt to drive the MCP contract and stop rather than improvise.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Project Home preflight refusal and a push-based generation completion signal
bodyPreview:
# Goal

"Generate My Project Home" today has no preconditions at all — useBuilderEpic.generate() creates an Epic and immediately sends, even when the persona is missing and the contract MCP is unreachable, which is exactly how a foreign machine ends up with a session that runs forever and a UI that never changes. Add a preflight that refuses with a real reason, and replace the one-shot pull with a push-based completion signal so a finished (or stuck) generation is visible instead of silent.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Prove the Project Home pipeline is self-sufficient on a machine that has only the npm package
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Close the loop on the cross-machine bug with a test that would have caught it. Pack the real tarball, unpack it into a scratch directory that is not this repo, and prove that everything a foreign machine needs to generate a Project Home is present and that the contract returned by the app is genuinely self-sufficient. This is the regression guard: without it the same class of breakage returns the next time a path moves.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Ship a guard-destructive-git PreToolUse hook so a shared tree cannot be stashed or reset by an executor
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`scripts/hooks/` ships exactly two PreToolUse guards (`guard-prd-writes.cjs`, `guard-inline-implementation.cjs`) — nothing intercepts `git stash`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git clean -fd`, or a blanket `git add -A` / bare `git commit -a` issued by a headless executor against a SHARED working tree. In-flight PRD 1096 rewrites `standards.md`'s rule into a prohibition, but that is prose the model may not weigh under pressure, and both the 2026-09-01 social-signals-trader incident (live trading config stashed and never restored) and the starry-night-ships incident of the same day (~1,400 lines across four PRDs stashed, three files deleted from disk) happened with a rule already written down. Add the enforcement lever that sits outside the model: a hook that refuses the call.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Heal terminal rows whose work landed AFTER the run window, and extend the reverify pass to 'failed'
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`reverifyNeedsReview()` (scheduler.cjs:4976) is the only self-healing pass over stale terminal rows, and it has two hard limits that leave real, finished work parked red forever. (1) `isRescanCandidate` (scheduler.cjs:4899) requires `status === 'needs_review'` — a row that went to `failed` is never revisited at all. (2) `committedInWindow(cwd, startedAt, finishedAt)` (scheduler.cjs:490) only looks for commits inside `[startedAt, finishedAt+60s]`, so the extremely common real case — the run wrote correct code, exited without a SCHEDULER_VERDICT sentinel, and the commit landed later (from a sibling run, a retry, or a human) — is invisible to the healer. Inbound feedback from /home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships (2026-09-02) audited 16 open rows and found 10 wrong in exactly this shape; e.g. PRD 171's work landed as 112d91e and 08f4857, PRD 147's landed in earlier commits, and each stayed red until a human diffed git log by hand. Widen the healer's evidence window to "any commit since the run started that touches this PRD's declared paths", and let a `failed` row be a candidate too.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Reclaim leaked job-worktree checkouts and their empty hash roots under /tmp
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Measured on this machine 2026-09-02: `/tmp/session-manager-job-worktrees/` holds 1133 per-cwd hash directories, 1125 of them empty leftovers that `removeWorktreeDir` never cleans (it removes `<hash>/<slug>` but never the now-empty `<hash>` parent), plus two real orphaned checkouts from 2026-09-01 in the starry-night-ships hash that were never reclaimed. `reconcileWorktreesOnBoot` only visits cwds it is handed, so a checkout for a project the app no longer tracks leaks its disk and its `git worktree` registration forever.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Queue-health drift sweep: distinguish 'gate never ran' from 'gate failed' and report per-project drift
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Two failure shapes are collapsed into one today. `reapDeadRunningJobs` classifies a dead run via `classifyRunOutcome` (reaperHelpers.cjs) into success/failed/no_result/unknown, then files everything non-success as `failed` with the outcome buried in a free-text `error` string. `no_result` (the process died or was SIGTERM'd before ever emitting a verdict — the gate NEVER RAN) is a completely different fact from `failed` (a verdict event exists and says error — the gate RAN AND WENT RED), yet a human reading the queue cannot tell them apart. Inbound feedback from /home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships (2026-09-02): of 10 wrongly-red rows, most were the former, and the auditor had to reconstruct each against git log because the row did not say which kind it was. Second gap: nothing ever reports aggregate drift, so a queue only gets audited when a human happens to notice. Persist the distinction on the job row and add a periodic sweep that reports it.

# Acceptance criteria

title: A PRD can request a quiet-machine lease so a timing-sensitive gate is measured without the scheduler's own jobs as load
bodyPreview:
# Goal

The scheduler is the dominant source of CPU contention on this machine, and some PRDs' acceptance criteria are wall-clock measurements (frame time, performance fences). Measured in starry-night-ships: loadavg 10.41-25.89 across 14 cores from the scheduler's own concurrent jobs, timing gates self-downgrading to non-enforcing, and at least one PRD deferring its central deliverable because it could not trust its own numbers. PRD 1066's per-project cap of 2 does not help — the contention is cross-project. Give a PRD a declarable `quietMachine: true` so the scheduler serialises it against every other job for its run.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Report a job's leaked descendants in run metadata and on the job row
bodyPreview:
# Goal

PRD 1065 (commit dd78ddc) made a job's descendants unable to outlive it, by sweeping the detached child's process group in childWithLog.cjs's handleDone. What it does NOT do is tell anyone a leak happened: a job can background a CPU-burning process, exit completed, and have the sweep silently reap it with no trace in run metadata or the UI. Add observability to the existing sweep so a project whose jobs leak repeatedly can see it instead of inferring it from ps. This closes ask 2 of four in the 2026-09-02 starry-night-ships inbound feedback; asks 1 and 3 already shipped as PRDs 1065 and 1085, and ask 4 (pattern-matching unbounded child commands) is deliberately rejected in childWithLog.cjs's own comment in favour of ownership-based reaping.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Guard fix-chain depth at the PRD authoring boundary, where hand-written -fix-fix-fix chains actually originate
bodyPreview:
# Goal

MAX_INVESTIGATION_DEPTH=1 (scheduler.cjs:4779) caps the scheduler's OWN fix-plan recursion, and its comment records it was lowered from 2 to 1 on 2026-08-31 because of starry-night-ships. But an audit of that project's archive shows none of its -fix-fix or -fix-fix-fix PRDs carry createdVia:scheduler-api - they are hand-authored by planner sessions and later legacy-adopted. The auto-fix cap cannot see them, and lib/prdCreate.cjs has no fix-depth check at all, so a human or planner can author 113-fix-fix-fix-<base> with nothing pushing back. Add the depth guard at the authoring boundary so the chain-depth signal reaches whoever is actually creating the chain.

# Acceptance criteria

title: PRD agentType field: structured persona routing on a PRD
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Add a structured, validated `agentType` field to the PRD write path so a PRD says WHO executes it rather than encoding that in English prose in Implementation notes. Today `scheduler_create_prd` accepts `tag` (work type) but no persona field, so the only way to route a PRD to e.g. dev-lead is a sentence like "Work as the dev-lead persona" — unvalidated, unqueryable, and honoured only if the executor happens to read and obey it. The asymmetry is already visible in the codebase: the cross-project conduit `feedback_open_session` DOES take an `agentType` parameter, and an Epic already stores `agentType` structurally (src/main/lib/promptSessionSchema.cjs:74, read back by src/main/lib/agentModelResolve.cjs). The PRD path is the one place where the routing is prose. This PRD lands the field and its validation only; actually launching the job as that persona is the follow-up PRD.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Resume-first recovery: requeue a stranded job with --resume instead of authoring a cold fix-plan PRD
bodyPreview:
# Goal

When a job parks in needs_review with verdict `uncommitted_changes` (work is on disk, the finish protocol's COMMIT step never ran), the scheduler discards that run's context and escalates to spawnInvestigation, which authors a cold fix-plan PRD that a fresh `claude -p` must execute by re-deriving state the original run already had. The original run's Claude session id is already minted and persisted (spawnJob passes `--session-id`, scheduler.cjs:3220; stored at :3778 as job.sessionId), and chatRunner.cjs:550 already proves `claude -p --resume` works here. Wire a resume-first recovery path that requeues the SAME slug against its own prior session with a short injected preamble, bounded to one attempt, evaluated BEFORE any fix-plan investigation may spawn.

title: Salvage a job's uncommitted work on EVERY exit path, including in-place (non-worktree) runs
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`scheduler.cjs`'s uncommitted-work salvage (`jobWorktree.salvageJobWorktreeDiff` → `<runDir>/<slug>.uncommitted.patch`) runs ONLY inside `if (worktree.ok)` (src/main/scheduler.cjs ~3769-3784). title: Worktree isolation must not switch OFF when the base tree is dirty — carry tracked WIP into the worktree instead of running in place
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`createWorktree` in `src/main/lib/gitWorktree.cjs:232` refuses to isolate a job when `isBaseTreeClean(cwd)` is false, and `scheduler.cjs:3585` then runs the headless `claude -p` executor IN PLACE in the shared working tree. That is exactly backwards: a dirty shared tree is when isolation matters MOST. On 2026-09-01 in /home/bilko/Projects/social-signals-trader this fallback put an executor into the live trading repo while the operator had an uncommitted edit to the live config `data/spread_config.json`; the executor ran `git stash` to get a clean baseline, the change was reverted, and the live trader ran the next market open on the old rules (stash@{0} `WIP on fix/trade-log-reconciliation-out-of-band-closes` is still there). `git worktree add` never needs a clean base — the only real reason for the gate (stated in the comment at gitWorktree.cjs:225-231) is that a worktree checks out committed HEAD only, so the job would not SEE the human's uncommitted WIP. Solve that directly: carry the base tree's tracked diff into the fresh worktree as uncommitted changes, so the job sees the same content it would have seen in place, while the shared tree becomes untouchable.

# Acceptance criteria
error: reaped: process gone, no success result in log (no_result)

title: standards.md: forbid blanket stash/reset in a shared tree outright, instead of sanctioning a "polite" stash
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/standards.md:86` currently tells the headless executor that stashing someone else's WIP is acceptable if it uses a descriptive message and restores it before exiting. That rule is what the 2026-09-01 social-signals-trader executor was operating under when it stashed an operator's uncommitted LIVE TRADING CONFIG and exited without restoring it — the third incident of this class in that repo (previous: 2026-08-25, PRD 477). "Stash politely" is not a workable contract for a headless process that can be SIGTERM'd, rate-limited, or reaped mid-run; the restore step is exactly the step that does not survive. Rewrite the rule as a prohibition with a real alternative.

# Acceptance criteria

title: Job worktree cap must never be lower than the machine-wide slot pool — wait for a worktree slot instead of silently sharing the tree
bodyPreview:
# Goal

`KIND_CONFIG.job.defaultMax` in `src/main/lib/gitWorktree.cjs` is 4, but `sessionSlots.cjs`'s machine-wide `claude -p` pool defaults to 5 and is user-adjustable to 10. title: Raise the executor's foreground Bash timeout so scheduled jobs stop auto-backgrounding their gate commands
bodyPreview:
# Goal

Every scheduled `claude -p` job inherits the Claude Code harness's default 120s foreground Bash timeout. When a legitimate gate command (a test suite, a build) exceeds it, the harness auto-backgrounds it and returns a tool result saying "You will be notified when it completes." In a headless single-shot run there is no later turn, so the notification can never arrive: the model waits, the run ends at exit 0 with correct code written but NO commit and NO SCHEDULER_VERDICT sentinel, and the job parks in needs_review. Reported from /home/bilko/Projects/starry-night-ships as the dominant failure mode across ~30 PRDs (14 hand-authored fix-PRDs, some of which failed the same way producing -fix-fix slugs; one run burned 3608s). The structural fix is to raise the threshold so the trap is not reachable for normal gate commands. The `claude` binary honours BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (verified present in /home/bilko/.local/bin/claude), and cleanChildEnv does not strip BASH_* keys, so the scheduler can simply set them on the executor's child env.

title: Scheduler reaper must not terminalize a rate-limited exit — route 429 deaths back to pending, never failed
bodyPreview:
# Goal

A rate-limited claude -p exit that gets finalized by reapDeadRunningJobs() instead of by spawnJob()'s own completion path is written as terminal 'failed', permanently wedging every downstream job in a dependsOn chain. # Acceptance criteria

title: A fresh 429 must always re-engage the pause — the manual-override cooldown must not suppress a rate-limit pause
bodyPreview:
# Goal
